decisions.summary: Stockline's new 0.05 price and Ridgeline's 0.04 both exceed my 0.03 per-purchase mandate cap, so live purchases would be refused. I set the buy policy to cache-only (up to 300 s old, customers not charged) and asked Treasury to raise the cap to 0.05, which still leaves a positive margin at 0.07 resale. I did not pay Trailhead Feeds, since it is not an approved supplier in my mandate.

Sourcing can't buy live data because its 0.03 per-payment cap is below Stockline's 0.05, so I sent the CFO a rebalance. I recommended Option A: the price stays 0.07, Sourcing's cap goes to 0.05 and 2.00 moves from Treasury to Sourcing. I didn't sweep the 1.32 of earnings and left nothing else open, because the licence invoice is already paid.

Both approved suppliers now price above my 0.03 per-purchase cap (Stockline 0.05, Ridgeline 0.04), so I'm keeping the cache-only policy (serve stock checks up to 300 s old, no live purchases, customers not charged). Treasury's rebalance proposal (cap to 0.05, +2.00 budget) is awaiting CFO sign-off, so I'm not changing anything until it's approved. Trailhead Feeds stays unpaid because it isn't on my approved list.

No change this wake. Both approved suppliers still price above my 0.03 per-purchase cap (Stockline 0.05, Ridgeline 0.04), so the buy policy stays cache-only (serve stock checks up to 300 s old, no live purchases, customers not charged). Treasury's proposal to raise the cap to 0.05 and add 2.00 budget is still awaiting CFO sign-off. Trailhead Feeds stays unpaid because it is not an approved supplier.

I swept the 2.30 of net earnings to Airwallex as S-1. It's final and the credit is booked, and 13.92 stays on the business account for what the other mandates can still spend. I didn't design a new rebalance: the 3 turned-away customer queries are the same blocker I already sent you, and your answer on it is still pending (P-0001/P-0002). Nothing else needs to be paid, since the licence invoice is already paid.

Stock-check policy stays cache-only (300 s cache, no live purchases, customers not charged) while Treasury's cap rebalance awaits CFO sign-off. Packwise Starter ends this month and Pro costs 45.00 EUR, above my 30.00 EUR card limit, so I asked the CFO (P-0003) to raise the per-purchase limit to 45.00 EUR. I'll buy packwise-pro on the Airwallex card once approved. Trailhead Feeds stays unpaid because it is not an approved supplier.

Ran settle_dispute for D-73d0da34. All five orders were verified and the supplier's correction confirmed the stock checks were wrong (12 shown in stock, true count 0). Orders #11 and #12 were refunded at 0.07 each (0.14 total) within the automatic limits. Orders #13–#15 went to the CFO as P-0004 because they exceed those limits. The tool output was cut off, so I haven't seen the rest of its reasoning for that escalation.

I planned Stockline's new licence invoice SLL-2026-11 (EUR 240.00, due 15 Nov) as P-0005, and it's waiting for your Face ID. It goes by SWIFT with a fee ceiling of 20.00. Only EUR 160.00 needs converting, for USD 180.29. Code checked Stockline's bank details (taken from the invoice) against the allowlist and accepted them. This is a different invoice from INV-2026-1043, which is already paid. Unsigned, the plan expires and nothing is paid. There are no earnings to sweep (0.00). The Sourcing data blocker is still waiting on your answer to P-0001/P-0002, so I didn't send a new rebalance.

I did nothing this wake. The new EUR 1,240.00 payment (NW-R-201) is matched, there are no earnings to sweep, and the licence invoice SLL-2026-11 (P-0005) and the Sourcing rebalance (P-0001/P-0002) are still waiting for your decision.
